## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `147feb83ff81ceb11b186d282df7b98897db1bce`

Reviewed read-only through `refs/review/pr-10503` (head re-read from the PR: `147feb83ff81ceb11b186d282df7b98897db1bce`, unchanged; one commit on the branch) against merge-base `8c929e6942cd4c8a0af8d378cfd38585bc53870a` with `refs/review/main` at `bc4efba7`. Every line number below is at the head. I did not run the tests; CI ran them (see ③). I made no GitHub writes.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff touches 5 sources, 2 new pin files and 1 changeset: +500/-10. Item by item:

1. **`PeoplePicker` row subtitle, gated — right.** `packages/fields/src/widgets/PeoplePicker.tsx:196-202` adds `readableSubtitleFields`, filtering `subtitleFields` with `!perms.isLoaded || perms.checkField(objectName, f.split('.')[0], 'read')`. Object: `objectName`, the object the picker queries (`sys_user` from `LookupField.tsx:1459` `objectName={referenceTo}`). Key: the path's first segment, which is the field the row reads on that object and the same name the existing `$expand` gate judges at `:181-183`. Fed to `PersonRow` at `:495` (was the raw `subtitleFields` on base). `PersonRow.tsx:78` builds the subtitle from what it is given, so a filtered-out path is not drawn.

2. **`PeoplePicker` row avatar, gated — right.** `PeoplePicker.tsx:203-209` adds `readableAvatarField`: `avatarField` when `!perms.isLoaded || perms.checkField(objectName, avatarField.split('.')[0], 'read')`, else `null`. Same object and key discipline as item 1. Fed to `PersonRow` at `:496`. `avatarField` has a default of `'image'` at `:133`, so `.split` never sees `undefined`.

3. **`SelectionTray` avatar, gated — right.** `PeoplePicker.tsx:601` passes `avatarField={readableAvatarField}` (was the raw prop). `SelectionTray.tsx:87` reads through `getPersonAvatarUrl(record, avatarField)`.

4. **`LookupField` search-variant chip avatar, gated — right.** `LookupField.tsx:1384-1390`: `chipAvatarReadable = fieldReadGate(perms, referenceTo, idField)` and `chipAvatarUrl(opt)` reads `drawn(avatarField) || drawn('image')`, where `drawn(key)` returns `opt?.[key]` only when no gate is loaded or the gate passes that key. Used at `:1402` in the `pickerVariant === 'search'` branch (`:1401`), which is the only `Avatar` draw site in the file (`:1409-1414`; the compact trigger draws no avatar). Object: `referenceTo` (`:320`), the referenced object, which is the object every other gate in the file judges (`:695`, `:772`, `:905`, `:999`, `:1084`). Keys: the configured `avatarField` (`:341`, `fieldMeta.avatar_field ?? avatarField ?? 'image'`) and the literal `'image'`, each by its own name. `fieldReadGate` (`:187-195`) exempts only `idField`/`id`/`_id`, which is irrelevant to an avatar. The base read at this site was `(opt as any)?.[avatarField] || (opt as any)?.image`, the exact expression the card names.

5. **Memo dependency arrays — complete, `perms` present.** `PeoplePicker.tsx:201` `[subtitleFields, perms, objectName]`; `:208` `[avatarField, perms, objectName]`. Every free variable of each memo body is listed. `usePermissions()` (`packages/permissions/src/usePermissions.ts:115-118`) returns a fresh wrapper of the context value, and the provider's value is re-keyed on `isLoaded` (`MePermissionsProvider.tsx:394`), so the memos re-derive when a policy arrives. The chip's `chipAvatarReadable` is not memoised at all (recomputed per render, `:1384`), which is cheaper than a memo and cannot go stale.

6. **Behaviour before the policy loads — consistent with the family shape.** All three `PeoplePicker` gates short-circuit on `!perms.isLoaded` (`:182`, `:199`, `:205`), and `fieldReadGate` returns `undefined` when `!perms.isLoaded || !objectName` (`LookupField.tsx:192`), which `drawn` reads as "not withheld" (`:1387`). Nothing is withheld until a policy loads. That is the `RelatedList.keepReadableColumns` shape (`packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx:802`) and the shape objectui#10411 landed. With no provider mounted, `usePermissions` answers the frozen `NO_PROVIDER_PERMISSIONS` with `isLoaded: false` (`usePermissions.ts:32-49`), so nothing is withheld there either; pin 6 of the PeoplePicker file and pin 5 of the chip file cover that leg.

7. **Null-avatar semantics — no ungated fallback anywhere.** A denied avatar reaches `PersonRow` and `SelectionTray` as `null`, not `undefined`. Their destructuring defaults `avatarField = 'image'` (`PersonRow.tsx:70`, `SelectionTray.tsx:54`) apply only to `undefined`, so `null` survives to `getPersonAvatarUrl(record, null)`, whose `record && avatarField ? resolvePath(...) : undefined` (`personDisplay.ts:65`) yields `undefined`; the `AvatarImage` is then not rendered (`PersonRow.tsx:106`, `SelectionTray.tsx:96`) and the initials fallback draws (`:107`, `:97`). The row and tray therefore do NOT fall back to a default `image` key when the configured field is denied. The chip does fall back to `image`, but only through `drawn('image')`, i.e. judged on its own key (`LookupField.tsx:1388`). The divergence the PR body names (row/tray stricter than the chip) is real, and both sides are safe: neither draws a denied value.

8. **Published surface — nothing moved.** `packages/fields/package.json` exports only `.` (`dist/index.d.ts`) and `./style.css`. `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` re-exports `./widgets/LookupField.js` (`:4137`) and `./widgets/UserField.js` (`:4156`) and does not export `PeoplePicker.js`, `PersonRow.js`, `SelectionTray.js` or `personDisplay.js` (grep at head: no such lines). `LookupField.tsx`'s exports are `LookupOption` (`:39`, unchanged, it already had an index signature) and `LookupField` (`:264`, signature unchanged); `UserField.tsx` exports only `UserField` (`:32`). So the three type changes in the diff, `PersonRowProps.avatarField` to `string | null` (`PersonRow.tsx:37`), `SelectionTrayProps.avatarField` to `string | null` (`SelectionTray.tsx:37`) and `getPersonAvatarUrl`'s parameter to `string | null` (`personDisplay.ts:64`), are on internal modules unreachable from the published `.d.ts` graph. `PeoplePickerProps` changed only in doc comments (`PeoplePicker.tsx:76-83`). No `.d.ts` shape that a consumer can import changed.

9. **Value path unchanged — right.** `commit` (`PeoplePicker.tsx:329-337`), `commitLive` (`:340-346`), `handleRowSelect` (`:348-369`) and `selectedRecords` still carry the served record untouched; only what is drawn is filtered. Pin 1 asserts `onSelect` receives `u1` after clicking a row with denied fields.

10. **Pins — match the card's pin and are not vacuous.** `PeoplePicker.outputFls-10433.test.tsx` mounts the real role-based `PermissionProvider` from `@object-ui/permissions` (`:81-98`), on `sys_user`, with a data source that does not strip denied keys (`:64-75`). Test 1 (`:165-176`) is the card's pin verbatim: `email` and `image` denied, row shows `555-0100` but not `amy@x.io`, no `img`, initials `AL`, click yields `onSelect('u1')`. Tests 2-4 cover a custom avatar field judged by its own name, a relation path withheld even when the backend expands anyway, and the tray. Both controls assert the `img` IS present (`:211-212`, `:221`), which is what makes the denial assertions falsifiable given the `LoadedImage` double on `window.Image` (`:125-133`, restored at `:161`). `LookupField.chipAvatarFls-10433.test.tsx` does the same through `UserField` (`:85-98`): `image` denied (`:146-152`), `photo` + `image` both denied (`:154-158`), `image` readable standing in for a denied `photo` (`:160-164`), plus two controls. Both suites run in CI's Test shards (all success).

11. **Card asks vs. delivered.** All three named outputs are gated (items 1-4). The card's pin is implemented (item 10). The card's optional residual (chip label falling back to `opt[displayField]`, `LookupField.tsx:1398`) is not done; the claim excluded it explicitly because it borders objectui#10343's label region, so it is not owed here. Nothing outside the card was done: the `null` type widening on internal props is the mechanism the card's fix needs (item 7), not extra scope.

12. **Residuals, disclosed by the PR, confirmed at source, outside the card.** (a) `PersonRow.tsx:77` and `SelectionTray.tsx:86` draw the person's NAME via `getPersonName(record, displayField)` with no gate, and `getPersonName` (`personDisplay.ts:24-28`) additionally falls through `record.name ?? record.username ?? record.label`, all ungated. The card names the subtitle and avatar only, so this is a new card, not a defect of this PR. (b) `UserCellRenderer` in `index.tsx`, another seat's surface. Neither blocks.

13. **Provider semantics note.** `PermissionProvider.checkField` answers `true` for an object with no policy entry and for a field with no entry (`PermissionProvider.tsx:105`, `:129`), so the objectui#7215 undeclared-key trap does not bite here; and the names judged are caller-configured (`subtitle`, `avatar_field`), exactly the names the existing `$expand` gate already judges. Consistent.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/10433-peoplepicker-fls-outputs.md` declares `'@object-ui/fields': patch`. AGENTS.md 版本号策略: never `major` (CI-enforced by `check-changeset-no-major`); objectui's own breaking changes are marked `minor`; ordinary fixes advance independently of objectstack. This is a non-breaking bug fix with no published shape change (① item 8), so `patch` is the right level. `@object-ui/fields` is in the `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, so the group takes a patch bump. The four changeset check-runs (`Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`) are success.

Prose, sentence by sentence against the diff:

1. "A lookup field that sets `picker: 'search'` (every user field does by default) opens `PeoplePicker`" — TRUE: `UserField.tsx:50` `picker: meta?.picker ?? 'search'`; `LookupField.tsx:1450-1451`.
2. "whose rows show an avatar and a subtitle line built from the field's `subtitle` paths, such as `primary_business_unit_id.name` and `email`" — TRUE: `UserField.tsx:51-52` defaults; `PersonRow.tsx:78-79`.
3. "Only the `$expand` those paths imply was filtered through field-level security" — TRUE: base `PeoplePicker.tsx` has exactly one `checkField` (the `$expand` memo); head has three.
4. "Once the permission policy had loaded, a row still drew every subtitle field and the avatar straight from the record the server returned, so a field the user may not read on the queried object, such as `email`, still showed" — TRUE: base passed the raw `subtitleFields`/`avatarField` to `PersonRow` (diff hunk at `:492-496`).
5. "The multi-select tray drew the same avatar" — TRUE: base `SelectionTray avatarField={avatarField}` (diff hunk at `:598-601`).
6. "and the field's selected chips drew theirs from the configured avatar field, then from `image`" — TRUE: base `LookupField.tsx` read `opt[avatarField] || opt.image`.
7. "Now, once the policy has loaded, a row leaves out each subtitle path whose field on the queried object the user may not read" — TRUE: `PeoplePicker.tsx:196-202`, `:495`.
8. "and draws no avatar image when the avatar field is denied: the initials show instead, and the row can still be chosen" — TRUE: `:203-209`, `:496`; `PersonRow.tsx:105-108`; selection path unchanged (① item 9).
9. "A path through a relation is judged by the relation field, so it is left out even when a backend returns the related record without being asked" — TRUE: `f.split('.')[0]` at `:199`; pin 3 uses `alwaysExpand: true`.
10. "The tray follows the same rule" — TRUE for what the tray draws (avatar only; it has no subtitle): `:601`, `SelectionTray.tsx:87`.
11. "A chip judges both keys it reads: the configured avatar field, and `image`, which it falls back to" — TRUE: `LookupField.tsx:1386-1388`.
12. "A readable `image` still stands in for a denied avatar field" — TRUE: `drawn(avatarField)` yields `undefined` when denied, then `drawn('image')`; chip pin 3.
13. "Before the policy loads, nothing is withheld" — TRUE: ① item 6.
14. "The records the picker hands to `onSelectRecords` are unchanged" — TRUE: ① item 9.
15. "This is defence in depth: ObjectStack's `FieldMasker` already removes the fields a user may not read from the rows it returns. The change matters for a backend that does not." — TRUE as the cited rulings state it (objectui#7230 records `FieldMasker.maskRecord` deleting denied fields); the card and its triage say the same. Not re-measured against objectstack here, and nothing in the diff depends on it.

No false sentence.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body flags, answered.** (1) "Consumer sweep not run because the public surface is unchanged": agreed on structural evidence, ① item 8; the four changed modules are unreachable from `index.tsx`'s exports and `LookupField`/`UserField` export signatures are unchanged. (2) "Residual: name drawn ungated": confirmed at `PersonRow.tsx:77`, `SelectionTray.tsx:86`; outside the card's three outputs; a new card, not a block. (3) "Not in this PR: chip label fallback": the claim excluded it; not owed. (4) "Residual: `UserCellRenderer`": another seat's surface; not a block. (5) "Divergence, row/tray vs chip fallback": real, both sides safe, ① item 7; the changeset describes the row correctly. (6) "Boundary: nested segment not judged on the related object": the same boundary the `$expand` gate has, since the picker does not know the relation's target; consistent with the family. (7) "Docs: none added": no existing page describes PeoplePicker FLS; nothing owed. The PR states no open questions.
